## Tabburrito sync / profile (deferred 2026-08-04)

Context: raised after the 2026-08-04 session loss. Settings are already a single
compact JSON blob (~0.8 KB on disk), so settings sync is genuinely small work.
Session sync is the risky part and is deliberately NOT bundled with it.

- [ ] [LOW · later · val:med · L · opus-medium] SYNC-1 | feature | P2 | status:deferred | Google OAuth + Drive `appDataFolder` **settings** sync. ^d-3faabc
  Scope: the `tabburrito` localStorage blob (`ui/app.js:40`) - muted, dark, notifyServices,
  notifyModes, unloadSeconds, dndUntil, resourceMode, profiles - plus `PortableStatePayload`
  (`src-tauri/src/main.rs:1081`: unload_seconds, service_urls, linkedin_sort, notify_tracked).
  Any future per-service on/off toggle lands in the same blob and syncs for free.
  Design notes:
  - Desktop OAuth loopback flow (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`); do NOT embed a client secret
    as if it were secret - desktop clients are public by definition.
  - `drive.appdata` scope only. `appDataFolder` is hidden per-app storage: invisible in the
    user's Drive UI and unreadable by other apps. Never request full `drive` scope.
  - Refresh token belongs in Windows Credential Manager (DPAPI), never in the repo,
    never in the synced blob itself.
  - Needs a merge rule for two machines editing concurrently. Last-write-wins on a
    whole-blob timestamp is acceptable here and much simpler than per-key merging.
  - Must degrade cleanly offline: sync failure is never allowed to block app start.

- [ ] [LOW · later · val:med · M · sonnet-medium] SYNC-2 | feature | P3 | status:deferred | Upload the encrypted session backup zip to Drive. ^d-184686
  Middle option discussed 2026-08-04: protects against another accidental deletion by putting
  `install/Backup-TabburritoSessions.ps1` output in Drive. Restores only on THIS machine -
  WebView2 cookies are DPAPI-bound to the Windows account - so it is disaster recovery,
  not cross-machine login. ~14 MB per snapshot; needs retention/pruning to avoid Drive bloat.

- [ ] [LOW · later · val:low · L · opus-high · owner] SYNC-3 | feature | P4 | status:rejected-unless-revisited | Portable cross-machine sessions. ^d-9d175d
  Would require decrypting WebView2 `Cookies`/`Login Data` and re-encrypting them for cloud
  storage. **Advised against 2026-08-04.** Anyone obtaining the blob plus key gets full
  authenticated access to WhatsApp/Messenger/LinkedIn/Bluesky/Calendar, bypassing 2FA.
  Also ~14 MB of constantly-changing binary SQLite. Only revisit with a hardware-backed key
  and an explicit threat-model decision.

## Clipboard paste follow-ups (2026-08-05)

- [ ] [MED · soon · val:med · M · opus-medium] PASTE-1 | bug | P3 | status:open | Pasting a SECOND image into a LinkedIn ^d-331f71
  post does not attach it; only the first lands. Two attempts failed:
  (a) appending by reading back `fileInput.files` — LinkedIn consumes the
  selection on `change` and clears the input, so nothing carries over;
  (b) tracking the pasted set in the page (`window.__tbPastedFiles`) and
  re-presenting it. Attempt (b) PASSED a jsdom test that simulated the
  clearing and still failed in the real app, which means the mock does not
  match LinkedIn's real composer.
  **Next step is observation, not another patch:** inspect the live composer
  (which element receives the file, whether a fresh input is mounted per
  image, what happens on `change`) and write the test from what is actually
  there. Single-image paste works — do not risk it chasing this.

- [ ] [LOW · later · val:low · L · opus-high] PASTE-2 | feature | P4 | status:blocked | Pasting an image COPIED from ^d-dbd647
  another site (e.g. Bluesky) does nothing. The clipboard carries only an
  `<img>` URL, and image CDNs commonly send no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`
  (verified for `cdn.bsky.app`), so the page cannot read the bytes. A
  host-side fetch works (verified: 127,646 bytes retrieved natively), but the
  delivery route tried — a Tauri capability granting service webviews IPC via
  `remote.urls` — **blanked every tab** (5331082, reverted in 88082ae) because
  declaring a remote origin IPC-enabled breaks page scripts under a strict CSP.
  Needs a different channel entirely. Copying within the same site works.

- [ ] [CRITICAL · now · val:high · M · opus-medium · owner] INST-3 | chore | **P1** | status:open | Code-sign `tabburrito.exe`. Unsigned builds trip Smart App ^d-60f875
  Control (os error 4551) on some machines and show a SmartScreen warning on first run.
  *(2026-08-13: ESCALATED P3 -> P1. Unsigned is no longer cosmetic — Defender's ML engine now
  QUARANTINES the binary as `Trojan:Win32/Bearfoos.A!ml` (Severity: Severe, ThreatID 2147731250).
  On 2026-08-13 13:21:56 it removed the exe, the Desktop / Start Menu / Quick Launch shortcuts,
  the running process, and the `HKCU\...\Uninstall\Tabburrito` key in one sweep — indistinguishable
  from a silent uninstall, and it cost an investigation to identify. The binary was unchanged for
  8 days; definitions 1.457.130.0 (2026-08-12 16:46) changed under it. A rebuild at 15:38 was
  flagged again within 12 seconds, so this recurs on EVERY build. Absence of an Authenticode
  signature is the dominant ML risk input. Current mitigation is a Defender exclusion on
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Tabburrito` + `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TabburritoBuild` — that is a local
  workaround on one machine, not a fix. Also submit the sample to
  https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/filesubmission so the FP is corrected upstream.)*
  *(2026-08-13, PARTIAL: signing plumbing shipped. `install/Sign-Tabburrito.ps1` signs the exe
  when a code-signing cert is present and otherwise reports UNSIGNED and exits 0 — it never
  claims a signature it did not apply. Called from BOTH `Install-Tabburrito.ps1` (on the staged
  file, before the move, so the exe is never briefly live unsigned) and `Update-Tabburrito.ps1`
  (on the build-dir copy, which is where the FP re-triggered). `install/New-TabburritoSigningCert.ps1`
  creates a local self-signed cert — NOT run automatically, since it modifies CurrentUser trust
  stores. STILL OPEN: a self-signed cert is local-only, is worse than useless on any other
  machine, and is NOT proven to stop the ML false positive. Closing this properly needs a real
  CA-issued certificate; the plumbing then takes it with no code change beyond -CertSubject.)*
  *(2026-11-20: the signing scripts were removed with the source-rebuild updater. Releases are now
  NSIS setup.exe files on GitHub, update-verified by a minisign key (tamper-proof), but still NOT
  Authenticode-signed - so SmartScreen warns on first install and the Defender ML false positive can
  still hit other users. A real CA or Azure Trusted Signing certificate remains the fix; it would be
  applied in install/Publish-TabburritoRelease.ps1 before the .sig is made.)*

- [x] INST-7 | bug | P1 | status:DONE 2026-08-13 | `2>&1` on a native command under
  `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` made SUCCESSFUL commands terminate. In Windows PowerShell 5.1
  each stderr line from an exe becomes a `NativeCommandError` ErrorRecord; with EAP='Stop' that
  is terminating even when the exe exited 0. Found when INST-6's fix made the updater reach its
  build step for the first time: cargo printed "Finished `release` profile in 35.86s" to stderr
  and the script died on a clean build. Three latent instances beyond that one:
  `Update-Tabburrito.ps1` `git fetch` and `git merge --ff-only`, and — in BOTH
  `Register-AutoUpdate.ps1` and `Register-SessionBackup.ps1` — `schtasks /Delete` (so `-Remove`
  crashed instead of being idempotent when the task was already gone) and `schtasks /Create`
  (where the `$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0` handler below it was unreachable, since any stderr line threw
  first). Fixed by discarding stderr natively with `2>$null` where output is unused, and
  relaxing EAP across the native call where output IS needed. Note `2>$null` is safe — it
  discards at the native level and never creates an ErrorRecord.

- [x] INST-6 | bug | P2 | status:DONE 2026-08-13 | The auto-updater never rebuilds for LOCAL commits that are
  ahead of origin, so locally committed work silently never reaches the installed app.
  `Update-Tabburrito.ps1:95` computes `$needsUpdate = $hasNewCommits -or $Force -or -not
  (Test-Path $TargetExe)`, and `$hasNewCommits` is derived purely from `git merge-base
  --is-ancestor $remoteHead $localHead` — i.e. only commits arriving FROM the remote count.
  When local is ahead, the ancestry test passes, `$hasNewCommits` is false, and the script logs
  the reassuring "Up to date (local is N commit(s) ahead of origin/main - push to publish)" and
  exits 0 without building. Evidence: `c50d3e6` (consent-banner suppression) was committed
  2026-08-12 09:17:48; the installed exe stayed on `026219e` (committed 2026-08-05 16:58,
  installed 17:04) through SIX consecutive updater runs that all logged "Already up to date"
  (2026-08-12 10:04:07 / 10:04:25 / 10:05:28 / 13:00:03, 2026-08-13 13:00:15 / 13:18:42). It
  only shipped on 2026-08-13 15:39 because a manual reinstall was forced by INST-3. The window
  happened to be ~1 day; it is unbounded in principle, since nothing in the loop ever closes it.
  Note this is NOT the same gap as INST-1 / R-0138 (which is "the remote->rebuild path has never
  been TESTED"); this is a path that does not exist at all.
  Fix direction: compare the manifest's `sourceCommit` against local HEAD, not against the
  remote — the manifest already records it, and it is the only value that says what is actually
  installed. Guard the rebuild so an unpushed dirty tree still cannot silently ship.
  *(DONE 2026-08-13. Decision logic extracted to `install/TabburritoUpdate.psm1`
  (`Get-TabburritoUpdateDecision`, `Get-InstalledCommit`) and wired into `Update-Tabburrito.ps1`
  as its only staleness authority. 15 assertions in `install/Tests/UpdateDecision.Tests.ps1`;
  the two that encode this defect were watched RED against the old logic first, then green.
  Also fixed here: a missing remote no longer exits 0 without building; a `-Remove`-style dirty
  tree is now recorded as `sourceDirty` in the manifest, since cargo compiles the working tree
  and the manifest previously claimed a provenance the exe did not have; and the update path no
  longer passes `-NoShortcuts`, so a Defender sweep's deleted shortcuts are restored on rebuild.
  Verified end to end: stale manifest + deleted shortcuts -> detected, rebuilt, reinstalled,
  shortcuts recreated, manifest back to HEAD, second run correctly silent (no rebuild loop).)*
